q-97410.name: Question 1
q-97410.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
q-97410.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $‖v‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot (2\cdot 2)+3\cdot 3+2\cdot (4\cdot 4)} \\  & =\sqrt{8+9+32} \\  & =\sqrt{49} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

An inner product on V=R3 is defined as ⟨x,y⟩=2x1y1+x2y2+2x3y3. Calculate the norm of the vector v=[234] under this inner product.

a
43
b
7
c
29
d
52
e
35
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector v with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖v‖=⟨v,v⟩.

Computing ‖v‖ using our definition, we get

‖v‖=⟨v,v⟩=2⋅(2⋅2)+3⋅3+2⋅(4⋅4)=8+9+32=49=7.

q-97418.name: Question 2
q-97418.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=2+t-{t}^{2}.$
q-97418.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=2+t-{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(0)=2,\,p(1)=2,\,p(2)=0.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(0)p(0)+p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(0)]^{2}+[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(2)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+0} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97418.html:
Question 2
?

Let V=R2[t] be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most 2, equipped with the inner product ⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2). Calculate the norm of the vector p(t)=2+t−t2.

a
2
b
6
c
32
d
4
e
22
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector p(t) with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖p(t)‖=⟨p(t),p(t)⟩.

Since p(t)=2+t−t2, we obtain

p(0)=2,p(1)=2,p(2)=0.

Computing ‖p(t)‖ using our definition, we get

‖p(t)‖=⟨p(t),p(t)⟩=p(0)p(0)+p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)=[p(0)]2+[p(1)]2+[p(2)]2=(2)2+(2)2+(0)2=4+4+0=8=22.

q-97715.name: Question 3
q-97715.problem:
Let $V=C[0,4]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,4],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{4}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=\sqrt{t}+1.$
q-97715.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(\sqrt{t}+1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t+2\sqrt{t}+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}+\frac{4t\sqrt{t}}{3}+t)|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =(8+\frac{32}{3}+4) \\  & =\frac{68}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{68}{3}}.
$$

⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=∫04x(t)y(t)dt.

Calculate the norm of the vector f(t)=t+1.

a
 23
b
 683
c
 563
d
 343
e
 323
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector f(t) with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖f(t)‖=⟨f(t),f(t)⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨f(t),f(t)⟩=∫04(f(t))2dt=∫04(t+1)2dt=∫04(t+2t+1)dt=(t22+4tt3+t)|04=(8+323+4)=683.

Therefore,

‖f(t)‖=683.

q-97722.name: Question 4
q-97722.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3).\end{aligned}
$$

Normalize the  vector  $p(t)={t}^{2}-3t+4.$
q-97722.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.
$$

Since $p(t)={t}^{2}-3t+4,$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=2,\,p(2)=2,\,p(3)=4
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),p(t)⟩ & =[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}+[p(3)]^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2} \\  & =4+4+16 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $p(t)$, we divide $p(t)$ by its norm $‖p(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{p(t)}{‖p(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}-3t+4}{2\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{12}({t}^{2}-3t+4)\end{aligned}

q-97722.html:
Question 4
?

Let V=R2[t] be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most 2, equipped with the inner product ⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3). Normalize the vector p(t)=t2−3t+4.

a
612(t2−3t+4)
b
24(t2−3t+4)
c
624(t2−3t+4)
d
33(t2−3t+4)
e
66(t2−3t+4)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector p(t) with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as ‖p(t)‖=⟨p(t),p(t)⟩.

Since p(t)=t2−3t+4, we obtain

p(1)=2,p(2)=2,p(3)=4

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨p(t),p(t)⟩=[p(1)]2+[p(2)]2+[p(3)]2=22+22+42=4+4+16=24.

Therefore,

‖p(t)‖=24=26.

To normalize the vector p(t), we divide p(t) by its norm ‖p(t)‖:

u(t)=p(t)‖p(t)‖=t2−3t+426=612(t2−3t+4)

q-97725.name: Question 5
q-97725.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
q-97725.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =3\cdot (2\cdot 2)+(-1)\cdot (-1)+3\cdot (1\cdot 1) \\  & =12+1+3 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{16}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-97725.html:
Question 5
?

An inner product on V=R3 is defined as ⟨x,y⟩=3x1y1+x2y2+3x3y3.

Normalize the vector v=[2−11] under this inner product.

a
1111[2−11]
b
66[2−11]
c
14[2−11]
d
24[2−11]
e
22[2−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector v with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖v‖=⟨v,v⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨v,v⟩=3⋅(2⋅2)+(−1)⋅(−1)+3⋅(1⋅1)=12+1+3=16.

Therefore,

‖v‖=16=4.

To normalize the vector v, we divide v by its norm ‖v‖:

u=v‖v‖=14[2−11]
